Hi Daniel — thanks for the fast heads-up and for the logs. We're actively investigating. Initial findings: a subset of edge hosts in us-west experienced increased queuing on the streaming worker pool coincident with a burst of long-running prefix-heavy requests (very long conversation histories + large context). That increased tokenization and KV cache pressure and produced visible pauses between streamed chunks.

Short-term mitigations you can try immediately (safe, reversible):
- Reduce client-side max_tokens per request from 1024 -> 512 to lower per-request compute.
- If you control request pacing, add a 200ms min inter-token delay to smooth bursts (clients that re-open streams faster exacerbate queuing).
- Enable the older streaming mode (non-chunked) for critical flows as a fallback: set stream_mode=legacy in calls — this trades slightly higher tail-latency but avoids intermittent chunk delays.
- Increase your client-side stream timeout to 45s (was 30s) to avoid premature session closure during transient pauses.

We're restarting a small set of streaming workers in us-west now and will push a config to throttle very large priors for a short window. I'll send a follow-up with timeline and what we changed.

For the record, we'll be creating a ticket and sharing a short post-incident verification run that you can run on your side to confirm recovery.

--
Markus Klein

Redwood Inference

Hi all,

Summary and current status:
- Incident window: 2026-02-18 09:05–09:26 PT.
- Root cause (summary): transient queuing on a subset of us-west streaming workers due to a burst of requests with very long priors (8k–12k token histories) that increased KV cache thrash and tokenization CPU.
- What we changed (short term): recycled 6 streaming hosts (host-uw-12, host-uw-14, host-uw-19, host-uw-21, host-uw-23, host-uw-27) and deployed a temporary request-size gate that rejects requests with priors > 8000 tokens with 503 + advisory for 2 hours while system pressure abated. We also enabled an internal smoothing queue for streaming chunks on the affected pool.
- Verification: we ran the verification script (link below) and measured median chunk interval returning to normal within 7 minutes after the host restart and rule enforcement. Firenet's telemetry shows error rate dropped to baseline.

Recommended actions for customers (we've already communicated these to Firenet):
- Short-term: reduce max_tokens to 512 or use server-side truncate for history when possible. Increase client stream timeout to 45s.
- Mid-term (prod hardening): adopt token-count preflight on client to avoid sending huge priors and consider small rolling snapshots of history instead of full-history attach. Redwood will publish guidance and a small SDK helper in the next week.

Attachments included: latency_logs_20260218.txt, stream-config-snapshot-20260218.json
Verification run: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cExampleLinkForFirenet-logs

- Customer-facing postmortem and a short SDK helper for history trimming to be published by 2026-02-26.
- Follow-up Q/A session with Firenet ops week of Feb 23 — Monica to own scheduling.

Daniel — please confirm on your side that the stream timeout increase and token truncation reduced visible impact on your clients; if you have any remaining slow traces, send them and we will prioritize.
